The company boasts a staggering Return on Assets (ROA) of 100%, vastly outperforming the sector benchmark of 1.8% [E8]. This underlying power is translating directly into the bottom line, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of 167% over the trailing twelve months [E14]. Conceded: the 5-year compounded profit growth sits at -1% [E13]. However, this longer-term lag is being shattered by recent performance, where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 216%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E36]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 0x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E7], sitting at a depressed 15% of the way up its 52-week range [E5] despite a micro-cap valuation of just ₹ 5.68 Cr [E3].

Pasupati Fincap Ltd presents a precarious investment profile defined by a significant valuation disconnect and deteriorating long-term performance. The stock trades at a P/E ratio of 47.3x [E1], which is more than double the sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6], suggesting the market is paying a steep premium for a company with a negative book value of ₹ -1.89 [E2]. This valuation is particularly difficult to justify given that compounded profit growth over the last five years has been negative at -1% [E13]. Furthermore, the stock is currently languishing near the bottom of its 52-week range, sitting only 15% above its low [E5], and offers no dividend yield to compensate shareholders for this volatility [E4]. Conceded: the company has shown a recent surge in trailing twelve-month profit growth of 167% [E14], an ROA of 100% [E8], and a price-to-book ratio that is technically 0x [E7]. Despite these recent metrics, the structural instability evidenced by a negative book value and a stagnant ten-year profit growth rate of only 7% [E12] underscores the high risk inherent in the current share price.
